params.why: the subtracted constant in the second expression must be a small positive number, so the minus sign in the stem is honest
the given angles must be a clean size and not a right angle, so the transversal is a genuine slanted line

constraints: a * x + b == c * x - d
stem: $AB \parallel CD$, with both lines drawn horizontally and $AB$ above $CD$. The points $S$, $P$, $Q$ and $T$ lie in this order on one straight line (the transversal) that crosses $AB$ at $P$ and $CD$ at $Q$, so $S$ is above $AB$ and $T$ is below $CD$. The points $A$ and $C$ lie on the left-hand side of the transversal, and $B$ and $D$ on its right-hand side. It is given that $A\hat{P}S = ({=a}x + {=b})^\circ$ and $D\hat{Q}T = ({=c}x - {=d})^\circ$. Calculate the size of $A\hat{P}Q$, in degrees.
solution: So ${=a}x + {=b} = {=c}x - {=d}$, which gives ${=k}x = {=b + d}$ and $x = \frac{{=b + d}}{{=k}} = {=x}$.
$A\hat{P}Q + A\hat{P}S = 180^\circ$ (angles on a straight line $SQ$), so $A\hat{P}Q = 180^\circ - {=v}^\circ = {=180 - v}^\circ$.
notes: Text-only advanced exercise in the style of book exercise 7.1 q3 (an equation in x built from angle-pair reasons on parallel lines), but with one transversal and a three-reason chain: vertically opposite, alternate, vertically opposite, then angles on a straight line for the final angle. The two given angles are the 'alternate exterior' pair, which the book does not name, so the student must chain the book's own reasons to see they are equal. Layout is stated in words (horizontal parallels, S-P-Q-T in order on the transversal, A and C on the left of it, B and D on the right); the relationships hold whichever way the transversal slants. Checked numerically with coordinates for v from 40 to 150. An alternative route (A-P-Q equals D-Q-P, alternate angles) gives the same answer, so the key does not depend on the route. Parameters are built backwards from x (a whole number 8 to 30), so the equation always has an integer solution and the answer is a whole number of degrees.
